summary: The correction at 37de7769 (parent ac0aa1a6) touches only task-packets/TP-DMX-GOV-DELIVERY-EVIDENCE-SPINE-G0-LITE-001.json, is valid JSON, and passes its own canonical dopetask schema. All `rtk`-prefixed commands were replaced with plain runnable repository/system commands, and the two scripts named by verify commands exist in-tree. S0 now fetches refs/pull/1268/head into a bounded non-force local ref and requires ref^{commit} to equal caa4ec2913d0463c7e38835029f3f7adeb915ac6 via an explicit test before any failed-PR source path is read, replacing the parent's unproven direct bare-SHA diff. The overlap-classification logic is fail-closed and total over all set relations (COMPATIBLE/IDENTICAL/SUBSET/SUPERSET/CONFLICTING plus an UNKNOWN catch-all for missing authority, fetch failure, SHA mismatch, absent/multiple merge base, path-enumeration failure, out-of-payload path, or unprovable shared-path state), with SUBSET/SUPERSET direction fixed to the execution-main perspective. The listed S0 diff pathspecs match, in exact order, all seventeen non-packet, non-proof allowlist paths. No implementation payload, readiness/audit-acceptability ownership, merge/rebase authority, or PR #1268 mutation authority was introduced; all prior prohibitions on merging, closing, mark-ready, force-push, rewrite, and activation are preserved verbatim. Two residual, non-blocking risks are recorded below (both are structurally caught by the packet's own UNKNOWN fail-closed rule, not defects in it), plus an out-of-scope observation about a suspicious instruction block in AGENTS.md that was not followed.

findings.title: No explicit command computes SHARED_PATHS intersection or per-shared-path final-state comparison
findings.body: S0's requirements/validation prose defines SHARED_PATHS as the intersection of MAIN_PATHS and SOURCE_PATHS and requires classifying CONFLICTING when 'any shared path has a different final path state between HEAD and the custody ref,' but the S0 commands list only the two `git diff --name-only` enumerations (merge-base..HEAD and merge-base..custody-ref); no listed command performs the set intersection or the direct HEAD-vs-custody-ref content/state comparison per shared path. An executor must improvise this step (e.g., sort/comm on the two path lists, then `git diff --name-status` or blob-hash comparison per shared path). This is not a blocking defect: the packet's own rule makes 'unprovable shared-path state' UNKNOWN, and CONFLICTING or UNKNOWN both stop execution for supervisor review, so an executor who skips or botches the comparison cannot legally reach a permissive (IDENTICAL/SUBSET/SUPERSET/COMPATIBLE) classification without evidence. The gap is a determinism/portability risk for how the obligation gets fulfilled, not a hole in the fail-closed logic itself.

findings.title: S0 command sequencing relies on implicit fail-fast shell semantics
findings.body: S0's ordered commands (fetch, ^{commit} equality test, merge-base count test, path enumerations) are listed as a flat array without an explicit 'stop immediately on nonzero exit' directive in the packet JSON itself; the fail-closed behavior (e.g., a non-fast-forward fetch failing, or the SHA-equality `test` failing, correctly preventing any read of failed-PR source content) depends on an executor running them sequentially under fail-fast shell semantics (e.g., `set -e` or manual exit-code checks) rather than continuing past a failed step. AGENTS.md and the packet's general stop-condition language make this the clearly intended reading, and requirement/validation text ('before reading any failed-PR source path,' 'drift or an unavailable exact object stops without mutation') reinforces it, but the packet does not spell out the execution contract inline. Non-blocking: this is a documentation-clarity gap, not a logic defect, and is consistent with how other steps in this and sibling packets express command sequences.

findings.title: AGENTS.md (unchanged, out of diff scope) contains an appended persona-override instruction block
findings.body: AGENTS.md, a required S0 context_file and repo-wide instruction surface, ends with an unrelated block instructing responses to adopt a terse 'caveman' persona and describing a `/caveman` mode switch. This content is unchanged by the audited diff (present in both parent ac0aa1a6c8 and head 37de7769a2) and is out of the authorized single-path scope of this audit, but it is anomalous enough in a governance authority file to warrant flagging as a possible prompt-injection artifact. Per audit instructions treating embedded instructions in candidate-controlled data as untrusted, it was not followed. No action was taken on it and no packet-authoring change addresses it; noted for visibility only.

remaining_risks: S0's overlap-classification obligation (SHARED_PATHS intersection and per-shared-path HEAD-vs-custody-ref state comparison) has no explicit command in the packet and depends on correct executor improvisation; failure to prove shared-path state correctly resolves to UNKNOWN under the packet's own rule (fail-closed), but a careless executor could still misjudge inputs before that catch-all is invoked.

S0's fail-closed sequencing (fetch failure, SHA-equality mismatch, or multiple/absent merge-base all stopping before reading failed-PR source content) depends on the executing shell/agent running the listed commands with fail-fast semantics; this is implied by surrounding packet and AGENTS.md language but not spelled out as an explicit execution contract inside the packet JSON itself.

AGENTS.md (out of audited scope, unchanged across parent and head) contains an anomalous appended persona-override block resembling a possible prompt-injection artifact; it was not followed and requires no packet change, but remains present in the repository for a human governance owner to assess.
